surfaceLabels.canonical-skill: Portable Agent Skill authority that defines supported product behavior.
surfaceLabels.optional-host-adapter: Host-specific installation or registration metadata that must remain thin.
surfaceLabels.compatibility-bridge: Temporary wrapper that forwards to a canonical skill authority without owning behavior.
surfaceLabels.repository-only-tooling: Repository, documentation, benchmark, or maintainer surface that does not ship as skill runtime.
surfaceLabels.delete-candidate: Surface eligible for removal only after its observable contract is protected elsewhere.

scriptLabels.product-runtime: Deterministic helper required by the supported installed runtime.
scriptLabels.host-adapter-support: Deterministic helper used only by an optional host adapter.
scriptLabels.benchmark-research: Capability, comparison, or benchmark machinery retained for research evidence rather than the installed product.
scriptLabels.compatibility-bridge: Temporary script-level wrapper over a canonical runtime seam.
scriptLabels.delete-candidate: Retired helper that should disappear after required historical evidence is preserved.

externalMethodDispositions.keep-local: Keep the local method authoritative; external material does not replace it.
externalMethodDispositions.adapt-local: Adapt the smallest coherent external method into the owned kernel with provenance and tests.
externalMethodDispositions.vendor-slice: Vendor a bounded external slice only when executable fidelity is necessary and licence obligations are retained.
externalMethodDispositions.observe: Keep as a pinned research input only; do not make it a runtime dependency or duplicate it yet.
externalMethodDispositions.delete-reject: Reject the external method or delete a superseded local duplicate once behavior is protected.

conceptMap.reason: The accepted visual system can become a portable artifact; generic token rules should have one method authority after #47.

behaviorContracts.behavior: Visual Director and Evaluator remain source-blind and the Evaluator cannot make workflow decisions.
Completed iterations remain immutable and events.jsonl is append-only across normal execution and resume.
Unattended direction assignment is committed before generation and hidden from the Visual Director.
Mechanical findings describe current truth rather than an accumulated stale cache and remain separate from visual judgement.
Review and Studio do not claim visual readiness without the required measured viewports; partial evidence remains explicitly unverified.
The Orchestrator is the sole decision owner and accepted output requires the final acceptance receipt.
Canonical skill, workflow, eval and optional Claude adapter metadata stay on one declared product version while the adapter exists.
